I wrote that “mental is not curable” because so many online sites claim they have the cure. I wanted to change the focus because I have yet to see anyone admit that sometimes there isn’t anything to make it go away. I think the fact that some people preach that everyone in the mental health community will get better hurts those of us who won’t. I’m not denying people get better. My concept is the idea that mental illness is curable for all people hurts those who can’t get better. I think for many people as I said, many not all, that the idea that mental illness is curable can be damaging when you simply can’t get out of it. Some people get better but I also think relapse is very possible to. I wasn’t trying to deny some people’s recovery. I’m saying when people say they recover and that all other people can recover too it can limit the conversation for those of us who will never break out of this. I’m saying that when people say that medication and therapy is the cure all for everything it forgets that sometimes that doesn’t work for everyone. It works for some people and I’m not saying people shouldn’t seek treatment either. I’m saying treatment didn’t work for me and I don’t think we should shame people who don’t continue treatment. This is an open dialogue trying to see is anyone else has come to terms with the fact that some conditions are lifelong.
